summary: Tested VOCCSYS iteration 3 features: email alerts on inquiry POST (verified 202 Accepted in backend logs), JWT-protected admin dashboard (/admin/login + /admin), inquiry CRUD with Bearer auth, Case Study section, YouTube hero embed, and FAQ regression. Backend: 12/13 pytest pass. Frontend: All critical flows pass. 1 security bug found (lockout counter split by proxy IP). 1 informational issue (YouTube video unavailable - owner embed setting).

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout uses request.client.host (direct TCP peer), but behind the K8s ingress multiple proxy IPs rotate (observed 10.208.133.66 and 10.208.133.69 in db.login_attempts within the same test). Each IP maintains an independent counter so the 5-attempt lockout rule never aggregates across real public clients. Lockout is effectively bypassable. Fix: parse X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP (first hop) when computing the identifier, OR key the lockout on email only.

action_items: Fix lockout identifier so it survives multi-pod ingress (use X-Forwarded-For first hop, or key by email only). Current implementation does NOT prevent brute force from a real browser-based attacker.

YouTube video u0iLiX1AXN8 shows 'Video unavailable - This content isn't available' in the hero modal. This is a YouTube owner-side embed/privacy setting on that video, not a code bug. User needs to re-upload or enable 'Allow embedding' on the YouTube video. (Informational.)
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 299-300: `ip = request.client.host` behind an ingress returns proxy pod IP, defeating the per-ip:email lockout. Must honor X-Forwarded-For.

server.py line 345-347: email send failure is swallowed with logger.exception but inquiry POST still returns 201. Good UX, but ensure monitoring alerts on repeated email_failed events; no retry queue exists.

rca of the issue: Lockout bug RCA: /app/backend/server.py line 299 uses `request.client.host`. In this K8s deployment, requests arrive through an ingress that proxies via different cluster-internal pod IPs (observed 10.208.133.66 and 10.208.133.69 for sequential requests from one external client). The identifier `ip:email` therefore varies between consecutive attempts, and each counter stays below the 5-attempt threshold. Reproduction: POST /api/auth/login with fake creds 6+ times -> inspect db.login_attempts and you see multiple identifiers each with count<=5, no locked_until, and 6th login still returns 401 (not 429). Mitigation: compute client IP from X-Forwarded-For (take first entry) or from X-Real-IP header, or drop IP from the key and lock per-email only (with CAPTCHA added if DoS risk is a concern).
